A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Gaussian Eigen Models for Human Heads. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and the methods, equations, tables and figures can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original NeRSemble reconstruction, reenactment and compression experiments in Tables 1–4, plus Multiface evaluations in the supplement.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds regressor-input ablations and additional compression results in its appendices.

M1.justification: The CNN generator, separate PCA bases for Gaussian attributes, photometric refinement with periodic QR orthogonalization, and image-feature/PCA/MLP controller are retained. Rewritten explanations and newly evaluated input variants do not establish a change to the proposed default method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate NeRSemble and Multiface, including novel views, novel expressions and cross-person reenactment. The new regressor ablations use existing task coverage; Multiface was already evaluated in v1's supplement.

E2.justification: v2 Table 5 and Figure 11 add comparisons against absolute-feature, EMOCA-only, DECA-only and EMOCA-regressed FLAME-input variants of the controller. The avatar comparator sets remain unchanged, including AG, GA, INSTA, PointAvatar and AvatarMAV.

E3.justification: v2 introduces controlled self-reenactment comparisons varying the regressor's input representation, with corresponding qualitative cross-person comparisons. The original benchmark splits, metrics, image resolution, default component count and CNN training budget remain unchanged. Omitted training and timing qualifications do not establish revised experimental procedures.

E4.justification: Appendix B.1, Table 5 and Figure 11 newly examine feature-source choice, FLAME expression inputs and absolute versus neutral-relative features. Table 7 adds compression sensitivity results. The existing component/resolution sweeps, Multiface examples and distillation demonstrations using AG and GA are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The standard deviations used for PCA coefficient ranges describe the representation, not uncertainty in experimental results.

E6.justification: The original Tables 1–4 retain their numerical results, although Tables 1 and 2 exchange numbers. v2 adds Table 5 results, including PSNR 24.2997 for Ours and 24.3065 for Absolute, and nine compression PSNR entries in Table 7. Table 7's relationship to the retained Table 4 is unspecified, so its different values cannot establish a same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 1 defines independent per-modality expression coefficients, replacing v1 Equation 6's identification of coefficients with entries of the eigenvalue matrix. v1's explicit two-sided orthogonality identity is also omitted. These revise the mathematical specification without adding a theorem or changing the underlying PCA/QR construction.

C1.justification: v2 reduces the introduction's contribution list from three items to two, dropping the CNN generator as a standalone contribution and presenting it as an Animatable Gaussians adaptation. Compact eigenbasis distillation and real-time image-driven animation remain the central claims.

C2.justification: v2 Section 2.2 explicitly excludes complete distillation of avatars requiring image-space refinement CNNs, including Gaussian Head Avatar and NPGA, which v1 included in its broad applicability discussion. It also clarifies the selected teacher's FLAME-tracking dependency. Existing limitations concerning global PCA control and subject personalization remain.

D1.justification: CNN training hardware/time changes from approximately 24 hours on A100 to 10 hours on RTX4090. v2 adds float32 memory accounting and a future code/model-release statement, but omits v1's regressor supervision and AdamW training details, Scikit-learn disclosure, and Table 3's qualification that FPS excludes EMOCA processing.

R1.justification: New Section 2.3 positions GEM against Gaussian compression through quantization and pruning, distinguishing static or time-conditioned compression from controllable avatars. Together with the deferred-rendering distinction and explicit attribution of the generator to an Animatable Gaussians adaptation, this substantially expands and refines the research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract and method exposition are extensively rewritten around distillation. Gaussian-splatting preliminaries, generator descriptions and training details move into appendices; the avatar-compression discussion also moves, and universality is integrated into Discussion. This substantially changes the narrative structure.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column presentation, with redesigned teaser and pipeline illustrations, extensively resized and relocated figures, and new ablation displays. Table 6 redisplays existing memory values, while Figures 9 and 12 duplicate the retained GA comparison; these are presentation changes rather than new experiments.

improvement.justification: v2 improves the focus and applicability discussion and adds useful regressor controls. However, it removes reproducibility details and the EMOCA timing exclusion while retaining the same FPS claims, and its additional compression table is not reconciled with Table 4. These opposing changes affect scientific clarity and reproducibility enough that a reliable net quality improvement is not established.
